headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: caveman’s MCP/file handling can feed Semantic Kernel’s broad plugin-backed context and filesystem surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md and memory files, while Semantic Kernel also uses MCP and can ingest application-defined files. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled content from A can reach B’s tool-use path. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman content is routed through an MCP server into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins
IF Semantic Kernel treats file or plugin output as instruction-bearing text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents for untrusted content
Add a strict allowlist for files Semantic Kernel may read
Prefix all cross-agent text as data, not instructions
Review one sample end-to-end message path for prompt markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; B reads and writes filesystem content and sends context to broad external model providers or MCP/OpenAPI tools. Shared workspace or shared memory can therefore expose A’s sensitive artifacts to B’s outbound calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default library deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or memory store
IF Semantic Kernel forwards file contents or context to external model providers or plugins
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory
Turn off plugin access for files containing logs or notes
Check one run for outbound payload contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses files, while Semantic Kernel supports multiple instances with shared state via memory store and can write filesystem content. Even without git or shell writes, overlapping mutable state can race on shared notes or memory-backed artifacts. The conflict is plausible by default when both are pointed at the same workspace or memory store.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same notes, memory store, or application-defined files
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or optimistic concurrency
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Enable file locking in the orchestrator
Serialize writes to shared memory
Inspect one conflicting file for last-write-wins behavior
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content and project notes, and Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can consume those outputs as plugin or agent inputs. If B treats A’s generated text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or rendered outputs. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this exact pair, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses caveman output as an input to another agent or plugin
IF B does not verify A’s claims before acting or rendering
mitigations: Require a verification step before downstream use
Mark caveman output as untrusted in prompts
Add citation checks for factual claims
Review one chained task manually
requires-engineering: implement confidence or provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: A touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while B handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials and may persist application context. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a modest compliance gap is visible: mixed retention and secret-handling practices could create policy friction if the same data class is shared.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman notes or logs and then passed into Semantic Kernel context
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two storage paths
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared notes
Document retention for each storage location
Separate secrets from general context files
Audit one sample deletion path
requires-engineering: align retention and subject-rights workflows
